topics.title: Radio Callers Discuss Tattoos and Titanic
topics.summary: During a radio show, callers discuss various topics including an encounter with a man displaying controversial tattoos, the success of James Cameron’s ‘Titanic’, attempts to secure funding for a new movie, and personal anxieties about financial security. Conversations range from admiring tattoo artistry to debating racial attitudes.

topics.title: Boxing Fallout, Tornado Damage, Clinton Tour
topics.summary: Following Lennox Lewis’s fight, Howard discusses betting odds and Shannon Briggs's performance while reports detail devastating tornado damage across Minnesota. Simultaneously, President Clinton continues his African tour amidst scrutiny regarding Paula Jones’ legal challenges involving a former Miss America, with claims of testimony about alleged sexual misconduct.

topics.title: Denver Taxi Death Investigation - Witness Contradictions
topics.summary: Following a taxi driver’s death in Denver after being beaten, residents of a high-rise building were questioned but failed to report the incident or call police. A woman denied involvement and claimed the president forced her into sex, while another witness provided a sworn deposition contradicting this claim; she subsequently fled the country.

topics.title: Hollywood Casting Mishap – Rosie & Harrison
topics.summary: During a conversation, hosts discuss the idea of casting Rosie O’Donnell in place of Harrison Ford for a film project, citing potential chemistry while acknowledging Ethel Merman's role in ‘Annie Get Your Gun.’ The discussion then shifts to Linda Kozlowski’s marriage and weight gain, comparing her to Roseanne, followed by commentary on Ed Burns and trends impacting television programming.

topics.title: Howard Discusses Finances and Controversial Movie Reviews
topics.summary: During a lengthy conversation, Howard discusses his financial habits with callers, including saving money and avoiding excessive spending. He then moves into reviewing several films – ‘Schindler’s List,’ ‘Dog Day Afternoon,’ and Spike Lee's 'Do the Right Thing,' expressing controversial opinions about their content and themes while referencing racial stereotypes.

topics.title: Radio Host’s Chaotic Broadcast
topics.summary: A man reports being robbed while simultaneously discussing a Jewish movie and complaining about an order, then attempts to sell racist catalogs including one from the KKK. He engages in bizarre conversations regarding impotency treatments, acupuncture, Woody Allen's fashion choices, and makes offensive remarks before transitioning into discussions of HIV research and erectile dysfunction medications.”} 35 words
